html:
The leading man of Athens for some thirty years. He was elected general almost every year and led through speeches in the Assembly, not through any office above the others.

  • He moved the Delian League treasury from Delos to Athens in 454 BCE and spent it on the Parthenon and the rest of the Acropolis.
  • His law of 451 BCE gave citizenship only to children of two Athenian parents.
  • His partner was Aspasia of Miletus.
  • His war plan against Sparta was to avoid battle on land, shelter behind the Long Walls and strike by sea.

That plan crowded the city just as the plague arrived. He died of it in 429 BCE. Most of what we know of him comes from Thucydides, who gives his Funeral Oration.
